title: Streamline Terraform IAM & networking module interfaces; bump GCP/AWS providers
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Why: Our current IAM and networking Terraform modules have diverged across clouds and teams, causing high friction for feature rollouts and repeated provider pinning work. Out-of-date provider versions (GCP 4.x -> 5.x and AWS 5.x -> 6.x) are preventing us from adopting newer resource types and are producing noisy diffs in CI. Scope: - Redesign module input/output surfaces for iam-* and network-* modules to a stable, versioned interface. - Remove duplicated resource logic between gcp-network and global-network overlays. - Bump GCP and AWS provider versions where safe, resolve any provider-driven resource renames. - Add automated provider-compatibility tests in infra-ci (integration: dry-run apply against test projects). Success metrics: - Reduce terraform plan failures caused by provider mismatches by 90% across workspaces. - Cut mean PR churn for infra changes (apply plan > review iterations) by 30% within one month. - Completed provider upgrade with zero critical outages and documented rollback path.
acceptance_criteria: New module interfaces published with CHANGELOG and migration guide in Confluence
All internal consumers (>= 6 repos) migrated to new interfaces or shims
GCP and AWS providers bumped in main infra repo and CI runs green on staging workspaces
No runtime regressions in staging networking after staged apply (monitoring & smoke tests)
Rollback documented and tested (state snapshot + plan to restore)

Mar 01: Begin provider bump in feature branch infra/provider-upgrade-2026. Bumped gcp provider to 5.1.0 and aws to 6.2.0 in a single commit to keep lockfile consistent

Mar 07: Encountered issue where google_compute_router_nat behavior changed; mitigated by keeping nat sub-block explicit in subnet_templates and adding acceptance test to validate SNAT behavior
Mar 09: Security review: IAM changes reviewed by Security (notes in PR). No secrets or key rotations required for this change.
